messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] P1 - Dedicated pool GPU pressure detected for tenant evermoor-prod. Pool dp-42 reporting 95% GPU utilization, avg queue length 1.2k reqs, 3m avg latency > 3s. Paging on-call: @alice.sre

alice.sre: I'm on it, joining bridge now. Can someone post quick customer impact?

frank.prod: Evermoor UI teams report increased 5xx and timeouts, some long-running batch jobs failing intermittently. They said response errors started ~09:12 UTC.

carol.am: I just pinged Evermoor AM and CE. They confirm their analytics job kicked off a large eval against our endpoint — they didn't intend to run at that scale. They're standing by. This is an enterprise customer with reserved capacity + burst rights in contract; we should follow the approval flow.

bob.infra: Quick datapoints from metrics: dp-42 has 20 GPUs, 18 pinned by evermoor-prod containers, queue depth peaked at 1.2k requests, preemption disabled for pinned tenants. Autoscaler didn't trigger because tenant is in reserved capacity mode.

bob.infra: Command I ran: `rictl pool describe dp-42 --json | jq '.tenants[] | select(.name=="evermoor-prod")'` returned pinned_gpus: 18, active_reqs: 1120, avg_latency_ms: 3120.

alice.sre: Thanks. Options on the table: (1) Approve manual burst to shared capacity (fast but consumes shared pool), (2) Evict lower-priority tenants from dp-42 (risky, collateral impact), (3) Apply short-term rate-limit/throttle to evermoor-prod (mitigates but will impact their jobs), (4) Ask customer to cancel the job.

dave.ce: Customer says they can attempt cancel if we can give them immediate guidance. They may need 2-3 min to cancel. If they cancel now, that likely relieves pressure.

eve.support: I've sent an urgent DM to the Evermoor CE with the cancel instructions and a direct link to the job. Waiting for a reply.

grace.oncallmgr: We need a decision quickly. Given SLA and contract, I'm OK approving a short manual burst if the customer asks us to — but prefer they cancel first. If they can't cancel in 5 minutes, approve burst for 30m with strict auto-throttle and billing note.

alice.sre: Agreed. Carol, can you confirm with AM/CE that they are trying to cancel and we have POA to take burst if they can't?

carol.am: Confirmed: Evermoor CE is attempting cancel now and gave POA to Redwood ops to enable burst if cancel fails within 5 minutes.

incident-bot: Note: Burst approval requires approval from oncall manager. React with :thumbsup: to approve.

grace.oncallmgr: :thumbsup: approving manual burst 4 GPUs for 30m if cancel fails. Conditions: enable strict per-tenant qps limit of 50 rps and fall back to model-compact for non-critical routes. Log billing as emergency burst per contract.

bob.infra: Executing command to allocate burst:
```
rictl allocate-burst --pool dp-42 --tenant evermoor-prod --gpus 4 --duration 30m --tags "emergency-burst,approved-by=grace.oncallmgr"
```
Applying temporary qps throttle:
```
rictl set-tenant-policy evermoor-prod --qps 50 --route-fallback model-compact
```

alice.sre: Burst allocated and throttle policy applied. Observability: queue depth down to 420, avg latency 890ms and trending down.

dave.ce: Evermoor CE confirms cancel didn't fully stop the eval but the throttle + burst prevented further failures. They're happy for now.

eve.support: Logged customer notification that we applied emergency burst + throttle. Notifying billing and legal teams per contract.

frank.prod: Temporary mitigations look good. We should open a follow-up action: (A) postmortem with customer, (B) prevent accidental large evals by adding an onboarding guardrail, (C) consider autoscale override for enterprise tenants that respects reserved pins but can request burst automatically with human-in-the-loop approval.

bob.infra: I'll capture the exact commands + audit IDs. Audit id: audit-1719152468-evm.

alice.sre: Creating incident ticket and assigning to eng-infra for follow-up and to solutions for customer debrief. Closing live mitigation; will keep thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:

carol.am: I'll schedule a post-incident call with Evermoor to go over root cause and billing.

incident-bot: Incident updated: P1 -> mitigated. SLA impact: partial degraded availability for 9 mins. Next steps: postmortem due in 72h.
